\section{Interpolation of square roots}

We construct integral combinations of square roots by interpolation. The interpolation weights cancel the low-order terms involving the fixed entries, leaving an explicit remainder. Bounds for these combinations give gaps between the last two entries when they are nonzero. We also bound the ranges in which these combinations can vanish.
recommended.reason: The section currently begins with six definitions before saying what the weighted combination accomplishes. A cold reader can reconstruct the cancellation only at lines 550–564 and must wait until the later lemmas to see why vanishing is a separate obstruction. This opening states the mechanism and its limitation without adding notation.
recommended.mathematical_contract: No change to any statement or definition. The cancelled terms are the nonconstant degrees 1 through m−1 in the weighted anchor sum, as shown in the partial-fraction identity. The term 1−f(xy) remains, so the wording deliberately does not claim cancellation of every low-degree term of L_m. Bounds and zero cases are those already proved for m=2,3,4. All distinctness, full-ring, equal-modulus, branch and size assumptions remain in place.
recommended.independent_check: Reconstructed the barycentric weighted sum and its constant term before reading revision_v2/agents/structural.md. Checked the new sentences against the exact identity and the later nonzero/zero alternatives. No numerical rerun is needed for this explanatory insertion.
recommended.title: Explain what the interpolation weights accomplish
